args.guideSection:
## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** February 7, 1791, from Albany County
- **County seat:** Ballston Spa
- **Parent jurisdiction:** New York
- **Population during period:** 45,646 (1850); 51,729 (1860); 51,529 (1870, a slight decline); 55,156 (1880), per the county's FamilySearch Wiki page
- **Economy:** Saratoga Springs' mineral-spring resort economy drew visitors and workers; the Hudson River/Champlain Canal corridor supported milling, quarrying and transportation trades — consistent with a stone mason's work
- **Ethnic composition:** The FamilySearch Wiki does not break out ethnic composition for this county; an Irish Catholic immigrant community is attested by the subject family's own presence in Saratoga by 1880
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist, Reformed Protestant Dutch, Presbyterian, Society of Friends (Quaker) congregations are documented from the 1700s-1800s (NYGenWeb/FamilySearch Wiki); Catholic parishes in the county fall under the Diocese of Albany, but no specific parish serving the town of Saratoga in this period was named by any tool result
- **Key historical events:** None specific to 1855-1880 named by the FamilySearch Wiki beyond the county's formation and ordinary 19th-century growth

## Boundary changes
- Saratoga County was created from Albany County on February 7, 1791, and its boundaries were stable through 1855-1880 — no further splits or annexations are noted on its FamilySearch Wiki page.
- Neighboring counties, per the same page: Albany, Fulton, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Warren, Washington. A family near the county line could have records in any of these, especially Washington or Albany County.

args.guideSection:
### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Marriages were first recorded locally (town/village/city) starting 1847, but compliance lapsed within a few years; statewide registration of births, marriages, and deaths began in 1880-1881, with compliance incomplete until 1913 (births) and 1890 (deaths) — [New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records). The county's own page gives 1880 for both birth and death registration, and 1908 for marriage, likely referring to when county-level marriage license records at the Clerk's office became reliably complete — [Saratoga County, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy).
- **What exists:** No dedicated civil marriage register is likely to survive for an 1855-1879 Saratoga marriage given the above. "New York, Marriages, 1686-1980" (FamilySearch collection 1680847, index only) and "New York, County Marriages, 1778-1848; 1908-1937" (collection 1618491) bracket but do not cover 1848-1907 county civil marriages well.
- **Where held:** Town/village/city clerks for any local records that do survive; Saratoga County Clerk's office for marriage, divorce, court and land records from 1791 forward; New York State Department of Health for anything recorded after 1880.
- **Gaps:** No systematic civil marriage record exists for this county 1848-1880 — this is the central obstacle to finding the Hanrahan-Ryan marriage through vital records.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic (or other) church marriage registers are the primary alternative; newspaper marriage notices; the 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage/mortality schedules (12 months before the census).

### Church records
